## Dataset Overview

For this specialization project, I am utilizing the **Our World in Data (OWID) CO2 and Greenhouse Gas Dataset**. This dataset aggregates historical, geographic, and economic metrics regarding greenhouse gas emissions, energy production, and population statistics across global nations and regions.

* **Sample Size:** ~50,000+ observations spanning country-level annual records from 1750 through recent years.
* **Primary Scope:** Post-1990 sovereign nation data (filtering out regional aggregations and missing historical records).

---

## Research Question

> **"To what extent does a nation's level of economic development (measured by GDP per capita) influence its per capita CO2 emissions and its reliance on renewable energy sources?"**

This question explores whether economic growth correlates strictly with higher carbon footprints, or whether higher-income economies exhibit a structural transition toward cleaner energy mixes.

---

## Hypotheses

* **Hypothesis 1 (Continuous Relationship):** Higher GDP per capita is significantly positively correlated with per capita CO2 emissions ($CO_2 / \text{person}$).
* **Hypothesis 2 (Categorical Comparison):** Nations classified into higher income tiers (e.g., High Income vs. Low Income) will exhibit significantly higher mean per capita CO2 emissions (to be tested via ANOVA).
* **Hypothesis 3 (Energy Transition):** Higher-income nations are more likely to achieve a high renewable share (>20% primary energy) compared to lower-income nations (to be tested via Chi-Square).

---

## Key Variables of Interest

| Variable Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `country` | Nominal | Sovereign nation or region name |
| `year` | Discrete | Observation year (filtered for $\ge 1990$) |
| `gdp_per_capita` | Continuous | Gross domestic product per person (International-$) |
| `co2_per_capita` | Continuous | Carbon dioxide emissions in metric tonnes per person |
| `renewables_share_energy` | Continuous | Share of primary energy consumption from renewables (%) |
| `income_group` | Categorical | Derived tier based on GDP quartiles (Low, Lower-Mid, Upper-Mid, High) |
